one_line.text: A commercial emotional-education organisation and collective publisher using psychology, psychotherapy, philosophy, art, and culture across books, media, therapy, and workplace programmes.

biography.text: Founded in London in 2008 by Alain de Botton with colleagues from education, arts, and culture, The School of Life developed from classes and talks into an international media, publishing, therapeutic, retail, and business-training organisation. Its stated mission is to improve calm, self-understanding, relationships, work, and fulfilment through psychological education.

background.text: The organisation describes its content as collaborative and draws on psychology, psychotherapy, philosophy, art, and culture. Its publishing arm turns the creative team's work into a coherent house voice across dozens of books and tools. An Emotional Education is an anthology of earlier School of Life Press and blog material, with eighteen contributors thanked and Alain de Botton formally credited and introducing the work.

expertise.text: Its practical expertise comes from sustained production of educational media, publishing, classes, workplace programmes, and therapeutic services around recurring emotional themes. This supports breadth, editorial consistency, and public communication. It does not make every collective claim a scientific consensus or identify which unnamed contributor has subject expertise for each passage.

perspective_and_limits.text: The collective favours a calm, reassuring, psychoanalytic, culturally literate voice and treats emotional maturity as teachable. The same organisation defines the need, publishes the advice, sells related tools and programmes, and provides therapy, so its claims require independent checking. Collective authorship also obscures individual responsibility and credentials unless a specific contributor is named.

selected_works.title: The School of Life: Collected Essays
